prompt:
A clean, straight-on photograph of a child's wooden PEG-AND-DISK STACKING TOY: a flat wooden base with THREE upright pegs standing on it, labelled A, B and C from left to right. The toy has 4 graduated round disks of different sizes and colours -- from smallest to largest the disks are: red (smallest), orange, yellow, green (largest). A disk may only rest on the base or on a LARGER disk (never on a smaller one), so each peg's disks are always widest at the bottom and get smaller going up.

At the START the disks are arranged like this:
    - peg A holds, from the BOTTOM upward: green, then orange
    - peg B holds, from the BOTTOM upward: yellow, then red
    - peg C is EMPTY

Now perform the following moves ONE AFTER ANOTHER, strictly in this order. Each move means: lift the single TOP disk off the first peg and drop it onto the second peg (it lands on top of whatever is already there, and it is always legal):

    1. take the TOP disk off peg B and place it on peg C
    2. take the TOP disk off peg A and place it on peg B
    3. take the TOP disk off peg C and place it on peg B
    4. take the TOP disk off peg A and place it on peg C
    5. take the TOP disk off peg B and place it on peg C

Work through the moves in order and render the FINAL state of the toy after ALL the moves above have been made: draw the three pegs A, B and C with their disks stacked in the correct order, largest at the bottom, in the correct colours, with the correct NUMBER of disks on each peg. A peg with no disks left should be drawn empty. Do NOT write the move list, the disk counts, or any numbers anywhere in the image -- the answer must be shown only by which disks are stacked on which peg and how tall each stack is.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show a wooden peg-and-disk stacking toy: a base with three upright pegs labelled A, B, C carrying graduated coloured disks (largest at the bottom)? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_count_a: Look at the peg-and-disk toy. Write down every disk stacked on peg A (the LEFT peg) right now, working from the top of that peg downwards, each with a few plain words saying how wide it is or what colour it is. Take only disks actually drawn on that peg. Separate one item from the next with a semicolon; write no running total and nothing else. If that peg carries no disk, write the single word NONE.
reference.q_count_b: Look at the peg-and-disk toy. Take only disks actually drawn on that peg. Separate one item from the next with a semicolon; write no running total and nothing else. If that peg carries no disk, write the single word NONE.
reference.q_count_c: Look at the peg-and-disk toy. Write down every disk stacked on peg C (the RIGHT peg) right now, working from the top of that peg downwards, each with a few plain words saying how wide it is or what colour it is. Take only disks actually drawn on that peg. Separate one item from the next with a semicolon; write no running total and nothing else. If that peg carries no disk, write the single word NONE.
reference.q_top_a: Look at the peg-and-disk toy. What COLOUR is the TOP disk on peg A (the LEFT peg) -- the smallest, uppermost disk on that peg? If peg A has no disks, answer 'empty'. Answer with a single colour word (one of: red, orange, yellow, green, blue) or 'empty'.
reference.q_pegs: How many upright pegs are standing on the base of this stacking toy? Answer with a whole number only.

steps.read_grid: the number of disks stacked on each peg, giving one whole number per row in the order peg A (left) on the top row, peg B (middle) on the middle row, peg C (right) on the bottom row

steps.target: upright peg standing on the wooden base of the stacking toy

steps.read_crop: Does this picture show ONE whole upright peg standing on the base of a toy rather than bare background or only part of a peg? Answer yes or no only.
